articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir deputy chief minister Surinder Choudhary hit out at the BJP over its demand for the dismissal of the Omar Abdullah-led
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir deputy chief minister Surinder Choudhary hit out at the BJP over its demand for the dismissal of the Omar Abdullah-led government, saying any attempt to interfere with an elected government would amount to an assault on democracy and the Constitution.Choudhary made the remarks after reviewing the progress of ongoing work at the new legislative assembly complex in Jammu. His comments came a day after BJP MLAs, led by Sham Lal Sharma, demanded the immediate dismissal of the National Conference-led government.Questioning the BJP's demand, Choudhary said the government had been elected by the people and asked what right the BJP had to seek its removal."If anyone can dissolve us, it is only those who elected us," Choudhary told reporters.He was responding to the BJP's criticism of the government after Chief Minister Omar Abdullah moved a resolution in the assembly demanding the restoration of full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.BJP accuses government of overstepping constitutional domainSharma had accused the National Conference government of attempting to revive an earlier political arrangement and challenge the constitutional framework.He alleged that the assembly resolution on statehood and related issues sought to revive matters linked to autonomy and the pre-1953 constitutional arrangement.Reacting to the demand for the government's dismissal, Choudhary said, "...this means you want to resort to hooliganism and use force and coercion. That is exactly what we have been saying -- that the BJP resorts to such tactics."He added that any attempt by the BJP to interfere with the functioning of the Jammu and Kashmir government or "block our freedom would amount to an assault on democracy and the Constitution".Choudhary also accused the BJP of being "anti-democracy, anti-constitutional and anti-public", alleging that its actions and statements were against the interests of the people."When you oppose a government elected by the people, you are going against those who voted for it," he said, adding that such conduct amounted to "treason".Deputy CM attacks BJP over assembly proceedingsChoudhary also criticised the BJP's conduct during the ongoing autumn session of the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly.He said the government wanted to focus on its work, while accusing the opposition party of prioritising political confrontation."They kept saying, we will corner them. But what did they actually corner? Instead, they themselves ended up in trouble after coming to the assembly," he said.Choudhary challenged the BJP to explain what it had done during the first three days of the session for the people."If the BJP is honest, let it tell us what work it has done in the last three days of the assembly session in the interest of the people," he said, accusing the party of carrying "bundles of lies".He alleged that the BJP had attempted to corner the government on social media but had failed to do so on the floor of the House, where issues could be debated through the constitutional process.Statehood restoration remains key issueOn the demand for restoration of statehood, Choudhary said the absence of statehood had weakened the ability of ordinary people to have their grievances addressed.He also accused the BJP of using police action against sections of society, including poor people, shopkeepers and journalists. He alleged that shops had been demolished and journalists who sought to publish reports critical of the government had faced pressure."If statehood is restored, I can say with confidence that these things will not continue," he said.Choudhary further alleged that journalists, employees, farmers and students were being prevented from speaking freely."If it were up to the BJP, they would impose Army rule across the entire country," he said, while alleging that the party's approach amounted to "hooliganism".Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A village in Egypt built a classroom with 9,000 plastic bottles after children had to walk over 2 km to reach school
articles.summary: Children in Ezbet Eshaq, an agricultural village in Fayoum, Egypt, once had to walk more than 2 km each day along a busy road in poor condition to reach
articles.body: Children in Ezbet Eshaq, an agricultural village in Fayoum, Egypt, once had to walk more than 2 km each day along a busy road in poor condition to reach the nearest school. A new classroom has changed that situation while also tackling another local problem of growing amounts of solid waste. Built with more than 9,000 reused plastic bottles filled with sand, along with earth, bamboo, clay and other reclaimed materials, the Eco Classroom was created with help from the people who would use it.The Eco Classroom helped children who walked 2 km to schoolAccording to the Holcim Foundation, Ezbet Eshaq is a rural agricultural village that was home to around 1,000 people when the Eco Classroom project was developed. The lack of educational facilities meant that village children had to make a daily journey of more than 2 km to attend the nearest school. Much of the route followed a busy road that was in poor condition.The project was designed as a practical response to that problem. Instead of bringing in a conventional building solution, the team behind the project looked at materials and skills already available in the community. The result was a learning space that also addressed the accumulation of solid waste in the village. The Holcim Foundation describes the building as an affordable and context-aware approach to providing safer education for rural children.What materials were used to build the classroomThe classroom uses more than 9,000 plastic bottles that were filled with sand and incorporated into the walls. Other parts of the building were made from locally sourced compressed earth blocks, bamboo and natural clay. Broken concrete from a nearby demolished clinic and reused sandstone were incorporated into the foundations.The approach extended beyond the main structure. Old doors and windows were refurbished for the classroom, while discarded wooden pallets were turned into desks and benches. Natural clay was used for plastering the floor, and bamboo formed the roof structure. The Holcim Foundation also reports that an anaerobic baffled reactor was installed to recycle wastewater for use in landscaping.The combination meant that waste was not simply removed from the village and replaced with newly manufactured construction materials. Items that might otherwise have been discarded were given another purpose within a building intended for everyday community use.Local people were majorly involved in its constructionThe classroom was not designed and built entirely from outside the village. The Holcim Foundation says the project began with design workshops involving parents and children, before extending to training for local young people in suitable construction techniques. Children and young people from the village, together with students from universities in Cairo, took part in weekly workshops where the plastic bottles were filled with sand.Ecogradia also highlights the strong community involvement behind the project. In its July 2024 discussion with Aya Helmy, co-founder and managing director of the BENAA Foundation for Sustainable Development, the publication described the classroom as a project shaped by children, parents and local youth from the beginning. Local young people were trained to assist with construction, helping develop practical skills within the community.That involvement also influenced what the finished space included. According to Ecogradia, conversations with children revealed a need for outdoor, play-based learning areas. These discussions helped shape the project around the needs of the people who would actually use it.What changed beyond the classroom itselfThe Eco Classroom became more than a place for lessons. According to the Holcim Foundation, introducing alternative materials and construction techniques increased awareness within the community about how buildings can affect both human health and the planet. Some residents subsequently requested that similar techniques be considered for their own homes.The building was constructed between January and June 2022 and is now a completed community learning space. The project later received an Acknowledgement in the 2023 Holcim Awards for the Middle East and Africa region. The Holcim Foundation's jury recognised its combination of recycled materials, low-cost construction, environmental responsibility and community participation.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2010, a rubber hose persuaded a retired athlete to found a footwear firm; 16 years on, it’s a multi-billion-dollar company that Kylian Mbappé signed with
articles.summary: A piece of garden hose may seem like an unlikely starting point for a global sportswear company, but that is where the story of Swiss footwear brand On
articles.body: A piece of garden hose may seem like an unlikely starting point for a global sportswear company, but that is where the story of Swiss footwear brand On began. In 2010, retired professional athlete Olivier Bernhard was experimenting with ways to create a running shoe that could deliver a different sensation underfoot. One of his early prototypes used pieces of garden hose glued to the outsole. The unusual experiment eventually became the foundation for the technology that helped define On's shoes and, with it, a company that has grown into a multibillion-dollar sportswear business.Sixteen years later, On has expanded far beyond its original running focus. In September 2026, French football superstar Kylian Mbappé ended his long association with Nike and signed with the Swiss company, becoming a global partner and shareholder as On prepares to enter the football market.The deal marks a striking new chapter for a company that did not exist until 2010 and whose first breakthrough came from a retired athlete trying to reinvent the running shoe.From athlete's experiment to a new shoeBernhard was not a conventional footwear entrepreneur. Before founding On, he had built his career as an elite endurance athlete. He was a three-time world champion and multiple-time Ironman champion, according to On's corporate history and its SEC filings. After retiring from competition, he became interested in developing a running shoe that could provide what he described as a new running sensation.The basic idea was to create cushioning that would soften the landing while still allowing a powerful push-off.His experiments eventually led to the prototype that used pieces of garden hose attached to the sole. The concept evolved into On's CloudTec technology, built around hollow elements on the outsole designed to compress on landing and provide a responsive take-off.Bernhard's experiments caught the attention of two friends, Caspar Coppetti and David Allemann. The three formally established On in Zurich in January 2010. The company says its early prototypes won the ISPO BrandNew Award in March that year, and its first shoes reached speciality running stores in July 2010.What began as a small Swiss running-shoe operation was designed from the outset around a simple idea: make running feel different.The three-founder modelBernhard brought the athlete's perspective, while Coppetti and Allemann brought experience in branding, marketing and business.Coppetti had worked in brand strategy and marketing, while Allemann had experience with advertising and consulting before joining On. The company's SEC filings identify all three as co-founders and describe their roles in developing the product, brand and business.The founders initially focused heavily on the running community rather than trying to compete immediately across every sports category. That strategy helped On establish an identity around performance running while gradually moving into lifestyle and other sporting categories.The company later expanded into apparel and tennis. In 2019, tennis legend Roger Federer joined On as a co-entrepreneur, taking an equity stake and becoming involved in product development. His partnership helped give the relatively young brand another connection to elite sport.From startup to publicly traded companyOn's growth accelerated significantly during the 2010s. The company expanded internationally and built a direct-to-consumer business alongside its wholesale network. By 2021, On was ready to enter the public markets.On Holding AG began trading on the New York Stock Exchange in September 2021 under the ticker 'ONON'. Its public listing gave the company access to capital as it continued expanding globally.The transformation is particularly visible in the company's financial figures. For 2025, On reported annual net sales of CHF 3.014 billion, up 30% from CHF 2.318 billion in 2024. Shoes accounted for CHF 2.804 billion of those sales, while apparel generated CHF 169.9 million and accessories contributed CHF 39.6 million.By September 2026, On's market capitalisation was around $10 billion, depending on the trading day and source. That makes the company substantially larger than the startup founded by three people in Zurich 16 years earlier.Mbappé takes On into footballThe latest expansion may be its most ambitious yet. On September 18, 2026, Mbappé announced his partnership with On after ending a nearly two-decade relationship with Nike. The French forward joined On as the company prepared to enter football, a market historically dominated by major sportswear companies such as Nike, Adidas and Puma.On's partnership with Mbappé goes beyond simply putting its logo on an athlete's footwear. According to Andscape, the deal includes equity and gives Mbappé a role in helping develop On's football products and strategy. The company has also appointed former France and Arsenal star Thierry Henry as its director of football.Mbappé said the attraction was the opportunity to help build something new with the company and contribute his experience to the products being developed.On is currently developing its first football cleats with Mbappé, Henry and Swiss footballer Sydney Schertenleib. The company says its football products are expected to become available in 2027.The first retail football boot has therefore not yet arrived. Mbappé's partnership is instead part of the product-development process, with prototypes already being tested.A very different kind of sportswear dealThe Mbappé agreement also reflects how On has approached partnerships with elite athletes. Federer's relationship with the company followed a similar model, with the tennis star becoming an equity partner and helping shape products rather than simply appearing in advertising campaigns. Andscape reported that Mbappé's agreement also includes equity and an opportunity to influence On's new football division.That makes the partnership notable because Mbappé is joining while still at the peak of his football career, rather than simply becoming the face of an established football-boot range.For On, the move represents a significant shift from its roots in running. articles.title: Bangkok under water: Torrential rain floods roads, forcing hundreds to evacuate- videos emerge
articles.summary: Torrential rain battered Bangkok on Saturday, flooding major roads, disrupting traffic and forcing hundreds of residents into shelters as authorities
articles.body: Torrential rain battered Bangkok on Saturday, flooding major roads, disrupting traffic and forcing hundreds of residents into shelters as authorities declared Thailand’s capital a disaster-affected zone.The deluge, which began on Thursday afternoon, left parts of the city under water, with some roads becoming impassable and vehicles partially submerged. Nearly 300 mm (12 inches) of rain fell in Bangkok within 48 hours, according to officials, Reuters reported.Thailand’s Meteorological Department warned that heavy rain and thunderstorms would continue across much of the country through Sunday, citing a strong low-pressure system over the central region and strengthening southwest monsoon conditions.Bangkok declares disaster zoneBangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the flooding posed a risk to lives and could damage public and private property, with areas near canals among the worst affected.Chadchart said floodwaters should recede once the rain subsides and that city officials were working to drain the water as quickly as possible.More than 200 shelters were set up across Bangkok, with around 900 people moving into them, the governor said. The army has also been involved in relief efforts, including setting up shelters and field kitchens.The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration designated schools as temporary accommodation and urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel.Roads flooded, businesses shutAccumulated rainfall in major Bangkok canals exceeded 20 centimetres (7.8 inches), officials said. Floodwaters spread across several parts of the city, particularly central and eastern areas.Phetchaburi Road, one of Bangkok’s busiest routes, was unusually quiet as vehicles were forced to turn back. Some cars were left partially submerged, while bikers were seen pushing their motorcycles through flooded streets.Many businesses remained closed on Saturday. Residents, some barefoot and others wearing rubber waders, waded through murky water while carrying food and drinking water. Some used plastic bags to protect their feet.Regional bus services from Bangkok to some eastern provinces were also suspended.Supermarkets were crowded as residents stocked up on essential supplies, while the government issued an emergency advisory urging people living near canals to move belongings to higher ground.More than 84,000 people affectedFlooding had affected more than 84,000 people across 21 provinces as of Saturday, particularly in central Thailand, the government said.Authorities sent emergency warnings through the cell-broadcast system to residents in affected areas. The situation also disrupted daily life for visitors and residents.Hwang Hwan-chung, who travelled from South Korea and has visited Bangkok more than 10 times, said he had never experienced such “crazy” weather and could not find a taxi.Sukanya Tongsuk, a local resident, compared the flooding with Bangkok’s widespread floods in 2011. "I think it's like 10 or 15 years ago that we saw heavy rain like this,” she told the Associated Press.Dutch resident Bjorn Franken, who has lived in Bangkok for two years, said he was able to cope with the flooding, although an event he planned to attend was cancelled.Airports operating normallyAir traffic control authorities said airport operations remained normal, although some flights could face delays because of weather-related route changes.Suvarnabhumi Airport was also operating normally, while Thailand’s tourism authorities advised travellers to allow an additional two to three hours for their journeys.Authorities continued to monitor the situation as heavy rain and thunderstorms were forecast over the weekend.Thailand had also experienced severe flooding in its southern provinces in November, when at least 145 people were killed and thousands of homes were damaged.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jharkhand Women Development Society partners with APNA to boost women, child protection services
articles.summary: Jharkhand Women Development Society partners with APNA to strengthen Mission Shakti, upgrade women’s helpline, and improve services at 35 One Stop Centres statewide.
articles.body: Ranchi: The Jharkhand Women Development Society (JWDS), under the state women, child development, and social security department, has partnered with a civil society organisation, Association for Parivartan of Nation (APNA), to strengthen women and child protection services across the state.The non-financial collaboration aims to improve implementation of Mission Shakti and expand protection, support, and safety services for women and vulnerable groups, with a focus on strengthening the state’s 35 ‘One Stop Centres’ (OSCs).A total of 11,151 women and girls received assistance at OSCs in Jharkhand from ??? to August 31, Mission Shakti data revealed.The partnership will support standardised case management protocols, standard operating procedures, beneficiary tracking, and grievance redressal across OSCs. It will also upgrade the women’s helpline, build frontline staff capacity, provide survivor-centred training, and coordinate Mission Shakti components through a joint state-level operational framework.Technology will be used through digital case management, beneficiary platforms, and real-time monitoring dashboards. The initiative will also include awareness drives on women’s rights and welfare schemes, policy research, technical advisory support, and coordination with police, health services, legal services authorities, rural development, JSLPS, and protection officers.Program director at APNA, Hunar Malik, said, “The collaboration would help translate policy intent into practical, on-ground impact by strengthening case management, training, and digital systems that directly support survivors and beneficiaries.”Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Seeing ‘account is on hold’ error on Netflix: Here’s why it happens and how to fix it
articles.summary: Seeing “Your account is on hold because of a problem with your last payment” error message on Netflix?
articles.body: Seeing “Your account is on hold because of a problem with your last payment” error message on Netflix? The streaming service says the error appears when it is unable to process the latest payment. It can happen if the payment method does not have enough available balance, has expired, or is no longer valid. A payment may also be declined by the bank, or the payment details saved on Netflix may not match the information held by the financial institution. Netflix users seeing error code E101 can update their existing payment method or add a new one to restore access to the service. Netflix also says it will automatically retry failed payments periodically during the billing cycle.What the error message ‘Your account is on hold because of a problem with your last payment’ meansThere could be a few reasons why this is happening:The payment method might not have enough money. (Pending charges or authorizations can affect the available balance on your card.)The payment method has expired or is no longer valid.Your financial institution didn't approve the monthly charge.The payment information given to Netflix doesn't match what your bank has on file.To get back to enjoying Netflix, you can update or change your payment method or contact your financial institution.How to update your payment methodYou can update your existing payment method at any time by following these steps:1. Go to the Manage payment method page. You may need to sign in if you haven't already.2. Tap the Update button to make changes to your existing payment method or select Change payment method to add a new way to pay.​Additional troubleshootingIf you’ve successfully updated your payment method, but still see the same error message, try clicking Back or Refresh on your device.If you can't update or add a different payment option, contact your financial institution or try paying for Netflix a different way.Note: Netflix will automatically retry failed payments periodically during the course of your billing cycle.You use AI every day.
